content: Desoximetasone is a topical medication prescribed to alleviate redness, swelling, itching, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It belongs to a class of drugs known as topical corticosteroids. The medication functions by activating natural substances in the skin to reduce inflammation, redness, and itching. Desoximetasone is available in the form of a cream, ointment, or gel, and it is typically applied to the skin twice daily. It is important to apply the medication at approximately the same times each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use desoximetasone exactly as directed. Do not apply more or less of the medication, or use it more frequently than prescribed. Additionally, do not apply it to other areas of your body or use it for other skin conditions unless instructed to do so by your doctor. This medication is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. To use desoximetasone, apply a small amount of the cream, ointment, or gel to the affected area of skin, spreading it in a thin, even layer, and gently rub it in. If applying the medication to a child’s diaper area, avoid using tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants. Do not wrap or bandage the treated area unless specifically instructed by your doctor. If your doctor advises wrapping or bandaging the area, follow these steps: 1. Soak or wash the area thoroughly. 2. While the skin is still moist, gently rub the medication into the affected area. 3. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap® or Handi-Wrap®). Secure the plastic wrap with gauze, an elastic bandage, or adhesive tape on the normal skin surrounding the treated area. Alternatively, plastic gloves may be used for hands, plastic bags for feet, or a shower cap for the scalp. 4. Ensure the edges of the plastic wrap are sealed tightly to adhere closely to the skin. If the area is moist, leave the edges partially unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. 5. Leave the plastic wrap in place for the duration specified by your doctor, typically no more than 12 hours per day. 6. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrap is applied. Do not discontinue treatment abruptly without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using desoximetasone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to desoximetasone or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention medications that suppress the immune system, such as azathioprine (Imuran), cyclosporine (Neoral, Sandimmune), methotrexate (Rheumatrex), sirolimus (Rapamune), and tacrolimus (Prograf). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have or have ever had diabetes, Cushing's syndrome (a condition caused by excess hormones), circulation problems, or any condition affecting your immune system, such as acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) or severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome (SCID). Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using desoximetasone, contact your doctor. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet. If you forget to apply a dose, do so as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double amount to make up for a missed dose. Desoximetasone may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Burning, itching, irritation, redness, or dryness of the skin Swelling, redness, or pus-filled blisters at the base of a hair follicle Tiny red bumps around the mouth Unwanted hair growth Pimples Some side effects can be serious. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: Severe rash Redness, swelling, oozing pus, or other signs of skin infection at the application site Children using desoximetasone may have an increased risk of side effects, including slowed growth and delayed weight gain. Discuss the risks of using this medication on your child’s skin with their doctor. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. If you apply more desoximetasone than prescribed or use it for a longer duration than directed, you may experience an overdose, which can affect your body in various ways. Contact your doctor if you accidentally apply too much medication, especially if you notice unusual symptoms. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your body’s response to desoximetasone. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
